sentences: Bandit combinatorial optimization chooses structured subsets and observes only the total loss of the chosen subset.
The source asks which properties of the particular action set determine its optimal regret.
General bounds in ambient dimension and subset size may ignore substantial structure shared by the feasible actions.
For shortest-path actions, the question becomes identifying graph properties that control learning difficulty, including on a simple directed grid.
A characterization would replace worst-case guarantees over all action systems with bounds that explain why one specific combinatorial decision problem is easier than another.
